project.description:
The Raft consensus core: leader election, log replication and the safety rules that make three machines agree on one ordered list of commands.
Note what this module does not depend on: storage. Raft's job is to agree on a list of opaque byte arrays. It does not know that those bytes happen to describe key-value operations, and it must never find out - otherwise consensus and storage can only be tested together, which is the mistake that makes Raft implementations untestable.
The node itself is a pure state machine: no threads, no sockets, no reads of the system clock. Time arrives as a method argument and side effects leave as returned values, sos a whole cluster can be drive by a fake clock inside a single-threaded test.
